newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state lawmakers seek gasoline tax increase.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state lawmakers seek gasoline tax increase.

text.p: Washington state senators on Tuesday proposed a two-step increase in the state gasoline tax that would fund $2.0 billion worth of highway and transportation projects.
The lawmakers are proposing an increase of five cents a gallon effective July 1 and want to tack on another two cents on January 1, 1998.
Washington's current gasoline tax is 23 cents per gallon.
The proposed increase would generate enough revenue to sell $2.0 billion of highway construction bonds, state officials said.

"All of the bonding revenue will go for construction, not operation or administration, so people can actually see -- and use -- what they are paying for when they fill up at the gas pump," state Senator Mary Margaret Haugen said.
Washington state last increased its gasoline tax in 1991.
Supporters of the tax increase argue that inflation and the greater fuel efficiency of late-model cars have eroded the buying power of gasoline tax receipts.
"It's pretty simple. Either we make an investment now, or we regret it later," said Senator Gene Prince, Republican chairman of the Senate Transportation Committee.
